events.name: Pentecost
events.description: The Spirit falls on the first disciples in Jerusalem; the church is born and the first thousands believe.

events.name: Neronian Persecution
events.description: After the Great Fire of Rome, Nero scapegoats and executes Christians; Peter and Paul are traditionally martyred.

events.name: Destruction of the Second Temple
events.description: Rome razes Jerusalem's temple; the church and synagogue decisively part ways.

events.name: Edict of Milan
events.description: Constantine and Licinius legalize Christianity across the empire, ending state persecution.

events.name: First Council of Nicaea
events.description: The first ecumenical council defines the divinity of Christ against Arianism and sets the Nicene Creed.

events.name: Christianity made the state religion
events.description: Theodosius I's Edict of Thessalonica makes Nicene Christianity the official religion of the empire.

events.name: Council of Chalcedon
events.description: Defines the two natures of Christ; the Oriental Orthodox churches separate over its formula.

events.name: Fall of Western Rome
events.description: The Western empire collapses; monasteries become the arks that carry literacy and faith through the upheaval.

events.name: Gregorian mission to England
events.description: Gregory the Great sends Augustine of Canterbury to the Anglo-Saxons, beginning England's conversion.

events.name: Islamic conquests of the Christian East
events.description: The Levant, Egypt and North Africa pass under Muslim rule; over centuries these heartlands become majority-Muslim.

events.name: Conversion of Kievan Rus
events.description: Vladimir of Kiev is baptized and the Rus adopt Byzantine Christianity, seeding Russian Orthodoxy.

events.name: Great Schism
events.description: Mutual excommunications formalize the split between the Latin West and the Greek East.

events.name: Fall of Constantinople
events.description: The Ottomans take Constantinople; Byzantine Christianity ends as a state and Orthodoxy's center shifts to Moscow.

events.name: Mission to the Americas
events.description: European contact and Catholic missions bring large-scale (and often coerced) conversion across the New World.

events.name: Protestant Reformation
events.description: Luther's Ninety-five Theses ignite a movement that splits Western Christendom and renews lay devotion.

events.name: Vernacular Bible printing
events.description: Luther's German Bible and the King James Version put Scripture into the hands of ordinary readers.

events.name: Peace of Westphalia
events.description: Ends the Wars of Religion with a confessional settlement, beginning the long separation of church and state.

events.name: Great Awakenings
events.description: Waves of evangelical revival sweep the English-speaking world, reshaping personal faith and reform movements.

events.name: Modern Missionary Movement
events.description: Protestant and Catholic missions plant churches across Africa and Asia; translation and schools follow.

events.name: Soviet state atheism
events.description: The USSR enforces militant atheism — closed churches, imprisoned clergy — yet faith survives underground.

events.name: Western secularization
events.description: Across the post-war West, affiliation and practice decline sharply as societies grow secular.

archetypes.name: The Unreached (antiquity)
archetypes.summary: Most of humanity in antiquity never hears the gospel; the dark warp behind the light.

archetypes.name: The Unreached (medieval)
archetypes.summary: Beyond Christendom's edges, the field stays dark for a thousand years.

archetypes.name: The Unreached (early modern)
archetypes.summary: Asia and the interior remain largely unreached before the missionary century.

archetypes.name: Born after the conquest (MENA)
archetypes.summary: After the 7th-c. conquests the Christian East becomes a shrinking minority.

archetypes.name: Confucian-Buddhist world (Asia)
archetypes.summary: Even amid modern missions, most of East Asia remains unreached.

archetypes.name: Hindu world (South Asia)
archetypes.summary: Christianity stays a small minority across the subcontinent.

archetypes.name: Apostolic convert
archetypes.summary: Hears an apostle or a neighbor, believes, and is baptized.

archetypes.name: Martyr of the persecutions
archetypes.summary: Refuses to recant; the blood of the martyrs becomes seed.

archetypes.name: House-church matron
archetypes.summary: Keeps a household church; the quiet backbone of the early church.

archetypes.name: Constantinian nominal
archetypes.summary: Joins when the faith becomes respectable; belief stays a label.

archetypes.name: Desert ascetic
archetypes.summary: Flees to the desert to seek God wholly.

archetypes.name: Barbarian baptized with the king
archetypes.summary: Converted top-down when the chieftain is baptized.

archetypes.name: Monastic copyist
archetypes.summary: Carries faith and letters through the dark centuries.

archetypes.name: Medieval peasant believer
archetypes.summary: Born into Christendom; devout in form, ordinary in fervor.

archetypes.name: Orthodox faithful of the Rus
archetypes.summary: Baptized with the Rus; Orthodoxy becomes the soul of a people.

archetypes.name: Thomas Christian of Malabar
archetypes.summary: An ancient church surviving on the Indian coast.

archetypes.name: Reformation lay reader
archetypes.summary: Reads Scripture in the vernacular and finds living faith.

archetypes.name: Recusant martyr
archetypes.summary: Dies for confession in an age of religious war.

archetypes.name: New World mission convert
archetypes.summary: Baptized en masse under colonial mission; faith folk and inherited.

archetypes.name: Hidden Christian (Japan)
archetypes.summary: Keeps the faith in secret across generations of persecution.

archetypes.name: Pietist of the awakening
archetypes.summary: Heart-religion rekindled in small renewal societies.

archetypes.name: Great-Awakening convert
archetypes.summary: Swept up in the colonial revivals.

archetypes.name: Mission-school pupil (Africa)
archetypes.summary: Learns to read Scripture at a mission school and believes.

archetypes.name: Slave-convert of the diaspora
archetypes.summary: Finds in the gospel both hope and a community in bondage.

archetypes.name: First reader of a new translation
archetypes.summary: The Bible arrives in the mother tongue; the church takes root.

archetypes.name: Colonial nominal Christian
archetypes.summary: Adopts the colonizer's religion as a label.

archetypes.name: Pentecostal of Azusa
archetypes.summary: Touched by the Pentecostal outpouring.

archetypes.name: East African revivalist
archetypes.summary: Confession and song turn a mission church into living faith.

archetypes.name: Base-community Catholic
archetypes.summary: Faith deepened in small grassroots communities.

archetypes.name: Soviet secret believer (Lyudmila)
archetypes.summary: Raised under atheism, lapses, then returns late through believing ties — the Lyudmila arc.

archetypes.name: Soviet atheist (lost faith)
archetypes.summary: State atheism severs an inherited faith.

archetypes.name: Chinese house-church believer
archetypes.summary: Comes to faith in a hidden church and stays despite pressure.

archetypes.name: Korean megachurch convert
archetypes.summary: Part of Korea's rapid 20th-c. growth.

archetypes.name: Western nominal who drifts
archetypes.summary: Inherited faith quietly thins to nothing.

archetypes.name: Post-Christian seeker who returns
archetypes.summary: After drifting, comes home through a crisis and a friend.

archetypes.name: Global-South migrant believer
archetypes.summary: Carries a vibrant faith along the routes of migration.

seed.name: Christ — Pentecost
seed.description: AD 30, Jerusalem. The single thread enters here.
